items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: We had Earl(?) Pernell on clarinet and saxophone. David Jones on tenor. Ernest Kelly on trombone.

ctx.x: Well, Joe Robichaux played piano. Joe Robichaux. Fats Martin on drums. We had Earl(?) Pernell on clarinet and saxophone. David Jones on tenor. Ernest Kelly on trombone. Ernest Kelly was a great man to play the Dozens. He'd actually talk about your mother in an uncouth

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Lee Collins and Ernest Kelly before David Jones. Went . . . played like 20 one- nighters

ctx.x: In the late ’20s, around 1928, you also did a little touring with David Jones and Lee Collins?

Lee Collins and Ernest Kelly before David Jones. Went . . . played like 20 one- nighters, and every one of them was a baza, which means it’s a bust-out, was nothing. They tell you, “You should have come here Thursday.” Thursday was payday. You come here on Saturday and Sunday or Monday, ain’t nobody. Nobody got no money. They spend up all their money. You mentioned David Jones, you mention a real giant. You never hear his name, but he was a real giant. He played tenor saxophone, played clarinet. His main forte…
